Additionally, this Sources Sought is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the Request for Proposal (RFP). This is a follow-on requirement. The current contract information can be found in paragraph 3b below. There have been no significant scope, magnitude, or complexity changes from the current contract. This is not subject to bundling or consolidation. INDUSTRY DAY/SITE VISIT INFORMATION: NAWCWD does NOT intend to hold an industry day/site visit. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE AND CONTRACT BACKGROUND The Government is anticipating this follow-on contract to be a Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Cost Plus Fixed Fee Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for Labor, and Cost Reimbursable CLINs for associated Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The estimated total number of labor hours is 278,800. The incumbent contract information is as follows: Incumbent Contractor: Computer Systems Center Incorporated (CSCI) Contract Number: N6893623D0018 Contract End Date: 06.10.2027 Contract Type: Single Award IDIQ with Cost Plus Fixed Fee Term CLINs for Labor, and Cost Reimbursable CLINs for associated Other Direct Costs (ODCs). Previous Set-Aside Designation: Not a Set Aside Level of Effort Hours on the contract: 280,050 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES Any anticipated special requirements and required capabilities are detailed in Attachment 1, Draft SOW. This document details security clearance requirements for personnel, facility requirements, and any specific certifications that are required for the performance of this requirement. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541330, Engineering Services with a Small Business Size Standard of $25.5 million. The Product Service Code (PSC) is AC12, National Defense R&D Services; Department of Defense - Military; Applied Research Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. title: Justification for Other Than Full and Open - Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � Texas
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded Contract No. 75D30126P21489 to the Texas Department of State Health Services for the Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System � Texas. The contract was awarded on a sole-source basis pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The requirement is for the identification and provision of Texas vital records necessary to support CDC's Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System. The Texas Department of State Health Services is the sole legal custodian and authoritative source of the required Texas vital records. Market research confirmed that the required records are maintained exclusively by the State of Texas and are not available from other sources in the required format. The contract includes a 12-month Base Period and four 12-month Option Periods. The Base Period value is $8,626.85, and the total potential contract value, $43,134.25. In accordance with RFO Part 6, the approved Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) is being made publicly available with this notice. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. The contract has already been awarded, and the Government is not soliciting or accepting proposals in response to this notice. This notice is being published solely to provide public notice of the award and the associated Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC).

title: Lease of Office Space in Fort Lauderdale, Florida - Request for Lease Proposals (RLP) #26NAT01 - Office Space
description: This advertisement is hereby incorporated into the Request for Lease Proposal (RLP) #26NAT01 by way of reference as an RLP attachment. The RLP can be found by visiting: https://leasing.gsa.gov/leasing/s/Offer-Resources The U.S. Government is seeking competitive lease proposals for new and/or continuing leasing opportunities through its online Leasing Portal. REQUIREMENTS City/State: Fort Lauderdale, FL Delineated Area (SEE ATTACHMENT): North: Route 834 to Highway 1 to NE 14th St to Atlantic Ocean East: Atlantic Ocean South: Atlantic Ocean to Eller Drive / Port Everglades Expressway / Highway 595 to route 817 to route 818 to Highway 75 to Route 869 West: Route 869 to Route 834 Space Type: Office (second generation, move in ready space required - space must be ready for occupancy by June 1, 2027) Minimum ABOA Square Feet: 6,345 Maximum ABOA Square Feet: 6,662 Parking: 15 reserved, on-site, secured parking spaces for Government Owned Vehicles Loading: Loading dock, freight elevator, or passenger elevator with ability to bring equipment in from the front or back entrances is required Layout: 3 separately demised suites consisting of 3,297 - 3,462 ABOA SF on the 2nd floor or above, 1,409 - 1,479 ABOA SF on the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd floor, and 1,639 - 1,721 ABOA SF on any floor. Colocation: Offered space cannot be in a building with the following other tenants: religious organizations, schools, daycares, substance treatment / clinic, marijuana sales, alcohol-only establishments, or residential (mixed-use) Lease Term: 15 years, 13 years firm Tenant Improvement (TI) Allowance: $54.24 per ABOA SF Building Specific Amortized Capital (BSAC): $12.00 per ABOA SF Amortization Term: 8 years for both Tenant Improvements and Building Specific Amortized Capital. SPACE LAYOUT (SEE ATTACHMENT) Block 1 USDA OIG - minimum 3,297 to ABOA SF to a maximum 3,462 ABOA SF - space located on the 2nd floor or higher required Private offices and workstations - 1,617 ABOA SF IT server room (requires 24/7 HVAC) - 140 ABOA SF Break room - 280 ABOA SF Conference room - 420 ABOA SF Equipment room - 210 ABOA SF Storage room - 210 ABOA SF Grand jury room - 210 ABOA SF Firearm storage room - 210 ABOA SF Block 2 FPS - minimum 1,409 ABOA SF to a maximum 1,479 ABOA SF - space located anywhere on the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd floors required Office and office support space - 545 ABOA SF Secure storage / weapons - 105 ABOA SF Tactical equipment storage - 84 ABOA SF Evidence - 105 ABOA SF Bulk storage - 105 ABOA SF Mission storage - 45 ABOA SF Canine training - 140 ABOA SF Canine hot bag storage - 140 ABOA SF CESM - 105 ABOA SF Vestibule - 35 ABOA SF Block 3 DCSA - minimum 1,639 ABOA SF to a maximum 1,721 ABOA SF - any floor is acceptable Private offices and workstations - 631 ABOA SF Interview room - 140 ABOA SF Reception area - 84 ABOA SF Conference room - 280 ABOA SF Printer area - 84 ABOA SF IT telecom room (requires 24/7 HVAC) - 140 ABOA SF Break room - 140 ABOA SF Mother�s room - 70 ABOA SF Contemplation room - 70 ABOA SF SPACE CONDITION The Government is seeking move-in ready / second-generation office space requiring minimal construction. This is intended to reduce TI cost impact and support the required post award schedule of reaching substantial completion and Government space acceptance by June 1, 2027. Minimal tenant improvements meaning the offered space has an existing office build-out and building systems in place, and the anticipated work is primarily interior improvements (e.g reconfiguration of non-structural partitions, finishes, limited MEP adjustments and device relocations, and associated fire/life safety modifications as needed). The Government anticipates some construction will be necessary; however, offerors must demonstrate the ability to meet the required Post-Award Schedule to be considered technically eligible for award and as, this is a low price, technically acceptable procurement, the final evaluated price will determine the intended awardee among technically eligible offers. POST AWARD SCHEDULE (SEE ATTACHMENT) The Government�s required post-award deliverables and timeframes are set forth in �Post Award Schedule� attachment to this solicitation. An offeror's ability to meet the post award schedule requirements is material to this procurement. To demonstrate the ability to meet Post-Award Schedule requirements, offerors must submit the following: Schedule Feasibility Narrative: As part of the offer, please include a narrative explaining the offeror�s assumptions, resourcing and approach for meeting each �Lessor Provided� post-award deliverable timeframe in the Post Award schedule, including (as applicable): long-lead items, A/E coordination, permitting/approvals strategy, QA/QC reviews and internal review/approval cycles. The narrative must identify key risks and the offeror�s mitigation actions. The narrative must identify any anticipated scope items beyond minor reconfiguration/finishes and limited MEP device relocations that could impact the critical path or the Post Award Schedule timeframes and explain how the schedule time frames will still be met. Evidence of Capability: If identified as the Apparent Successful Offeror, the offeror must submit the following items in addition to those required by Section 3.06 of the RLP prior to award. Identification of A/E and at least two General Contractors that will participate in the bidding process (or if not yet under contract, a firm plan for engagement and a letter of commitment from the proposed firm(s). To be found technically acceptable, the offeror must take no exception to the Post Award Schedule deliverables and timeframes and submit the two items identified above in a manner that provides a credible basis to conclude the Offeror can meet the required deliverable timeframes within the contracting officer�s sole discretion. Failure to submit these items or submission that is materially incomplete/conditional, may result in a finding of �Technically Unacceptable� FURNITURE The Government will accept offered space that includes existing systems furniture and furnishings (e.g workstations, private office furnishings, conference tables and chairs) for Government use to help support timely occupancy, at no additional cost to the Government. Furniture is not a requirement of technical acceptability and will not be evaluated for award. Offers that do not include furniture remain fully eligible. Condition Standard: Any furniture offered must be clean and in good working order with no significant defects, and available for Government use by occupancy as determined in the Government�s sole discretion. Furniture offered is subject to Government inspection at turnover/occupancy. If the Government will not accept the offered furniture, the Lessor bears the cost to remove it. HOW TO OFFER The Leasing Portal (https://leasing.gsa.gov) enables interested parties to offer space to the Federal Government through a secure, web-based process. To participate, register on the site by selecting �Register to Offer Space� and follow the instructions provided. Helpful resources�including instructional guides and video tutorials�are available on the portal under the Resources tab. Lease award will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer without negotiations. Offered space must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local jurisdiction requirements, including standards for fire and life safety, accessibility, seismic resilience, and energy efficiency. OFFER SUBMISSION OPEN PERIOD The offer submission window is between October 1 - October 16, 2026 (closes at 8:00PM EST on October 16th) REQUIRED SUBMITTALS BY OFFER SUBMISSION DEADLINE Post Award Schedule Feasibility Narrative Photos of offered space PDF and CAD floor plan of offered space Proof of authorization to represent the owner, or proof of ownership or control, as applicable IMPORTANT NOTES Please review Section 889 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) r

title: Czechia – Flow-measuring equipment – Hydrometrická přístrojová technika
description: Zadávací řízení je realizováno za účelem uzavření smlouvy mezi zadavatelem a vybraným dodavatelem, jejímž předmětem je dodávka hydrometrické přístrojové techniky a souvisejících podpůrných přístrojů. Veřejná zakázka je rozdělena na 7 částí. Součástí plnění je zejména dodávka požadované techniky včetně veškerého nezbytného příslušenství, dokumentace a uživatelských manuálů v anglickém jazyce, včetně jejich prostého překladu do českého jazyka, doprava do místa plnění, seznámení obsluhy s dodanou technikou a poskytnutí záruky na hardware a software. Zadavatel dále požaduje, aby součástí plnění bylo poskytování záručního servisu na dodaná zařízení po dobu nejméně 24 měsíců. Podrobná specifikace předmětu plnění veřejné zakázky je uvedena v této zadávací dokumentaci a jejích přílohách. Financování: Veřejná zakázka je ze 100 % financována Evropskou unií prostřednictvím Operačního programu životního prostředí („Dotační program“) v rámci projektu „Modernizace předpovědních systémů ČHMÚ II“ (reg. číslo projektu CZ.05.01.03/05/25_088/0006343) („Projekt“).

title: Spain – Research and experimental development services – Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)
description: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems.

title: Contingency Transportation Services BPA
description: This Notice is prepared in accordance with RFO 5.1 and RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. The Government intends to solicit this requirement directly from qualified suppliers in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2) for a firm-fixed-price contract as outlined in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). This Notice is issued solely for informational and market research planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, bid guarantee, or promise of contract award. The Government reserves the right to cancel or amend this procurement at any time. The Government is not responsible for, nor will it reimburse, any costs incurred by interested vendors or commercial entities in the preparation, compilation, or submission of responses to this Pre-Solicitation Notice. All participation is strictly voluntary and at the vendor's sole expense. REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW & SCOPE OF WORK The 356th Expeditionary Theater Support Group (ETSG) requires reliable, responsive, and secure commercial line haul and heavy equipment transport services across various military installations and port facilities on the island of Guam. Key performance parameters include: Service Scope: Safe transport, line haul, and handling of tactical/non-tactical vehicles, tracked heavy machinery (e.g., bulldozers, excavators), associated gear, and general freight cargo. Key Operational Locations: Performance involves transportation services to, from, and between Andersen Air Force Base (AAFB), Naval Station (NAVSTA) Guam Port Operations (Apra Harbor), Jose D. Leon Guerrero Commercial Port (Piti), Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport (GUM), and designated commercial or military maintenance yards. Notice and Scheduling: Standard transport requirements will be scheduled with a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours advanced notice. Emergency transport requests with less than 96 hours notice must be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. Equipment and Cargo Securement: 100% compliance with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) standards is required. The Contractor must utilize Grade 70 or Grade 80 transport chains paired with ratchet binders (lever binders are prohibited). Proper shoring, bracing, blocking, and cribbing (using heavy-duty hardwood timbers or composite pads) must be used to protect trailer decks and secure loads. Permits and Deliverables: The Contractor must obtain and submit digital PDF copies of Department of Public Works (DPW) Oversized/Overweight Permits to the 356th ETSG COR prior to dispatching any heavy or oversized movements. Personnel and Base Access: All vehicle and equipment operators must hold valid Territory of Guam Commercial Driver's Licenses (CDL) and federal DOT certifications. Personnel must pass background checks to obtain Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentials for base access, sponsored by the Government. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS FOR INTERESTED VENDORS Please reply to this Notice if your company is interested in participating in this upcoming solicitation. Responses must be sent via email to the Point of Contact listed below. Responses must include the following information: Company Details: Official Company Name, physical address, SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI), and CAGE Code. (Active registration in SAM.gov is required). Fleet & Equipment Capabilities: A statement confirming your firm's available heavy-haul assets (e.g., flatbeds, lowboys) and securement hardware meeting the PWS standards. Licensing & Base Access Compliance: Confirmation that all proposed operators hold valid Guam CDL licenses and are capable of passing background checks to obtain DBIDS credentials. Permitting Capability: Confirmation of your firm's ability to coordinate and secure necessary DPW Oversized/Overweight Permits on Guam. Performance Capability Statement: A brief summary (not to exceed 2 pages) of relevant performance history, local logistics capabilities in Guam, and past performance with commercial or military port clearance. Please review the attached PWS for additional details.

buyer: European Commission, FPI - Service for Foreign Policy Instruments
title: Canada – Public relations services – Policy Dialogue and Public Diplomacy Facility for Canada
description: The purpose of this procurement is to procure services that strengthen and deepen EU–Canada relations on key priority themes of shared strategic interest, while advancing EU interests and values in Canada through targeted policy dialogue and public diplomacy. The contract will support the implementation of commitments under the EU–Canada Strategic Partnership Agreement (SPA), the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and, where relevant, other bilateral frameworks including the EU–Canada Green Alliance and the EU–Canada Security and Defence Partnership. The procured services shall comprise two complementary components: Policy Dialogue Support — facilitation of structured policy dialogues across a wide range of areas through concrete activities linked to existing and emerging dialogue mechanisms, including joint committees and working groups involving the EU Delegation and relevant EU services. Public Diplomacy Actions — Design and delivery of public diplomacy initiatives aimed at increasing understanding of EU policies and priorities among Canadian audiences, demonstrating the tangible benefits of the EU–Canada partnership, and strengthening engagement with key Canadian stakeholders beyond government — including media, academia, civil society, youth, and opinion leaders. The services shall deliver measurable policy outcomes, consolidate trusted stakeholder networks, and amplify EU positions across Canada. Through the combined effect of policy dialogue and public diplomacy, the procurement aims to enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in Canada and contribute to closer alignment between EU and Canadian policy positions and approaches, including in multilateral fora, on major foreign policy priorities.

description: The purpose of this procurement is to procure services that strengthen and deepen EU–Canada relations on key priority themes of shared strategic interest, while advancing EU interests and values in Canada through targeted policy dialogue and public diplomacy. The contract will support the implementation of commitments under the EU–Canada Strategic Partnership Agreement (SPA), the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and, where relevant, other bilateral frameworks including the EU–Canada Green Alliance and the EU–Canada Security and Defence Partnership. The procured services shall comprise two complementary components: Policy Dialogue Support — facilitation of structured policy dialogues across a wide range of areas through concrete activities linked to existing and emerging dialogue mechanisms, including joint committees and working groups involving the EU Delegation and relevant EU services. Public Diplomacy Actions — Design and delivery of public diplomacy initiatives aimed at increasing understanding of EU policies and priorities among Canadian audiences, demonstrating the tangible benefits of the EU–Canada partnership, and strengthening engagement with key Canadian stakeholders beyond government — including media, academia, civil society, youth, and opinion leaders. The services shall deliver measurable policy outcomes, consolidate trusted stakeholder networks, and amplify EU positions across Canada. Through the combined effect of policy dialogue and public diplomacy, the procurement aims to enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in Canada and contribute to closer alignment between EU and Canadian policy positions and approaches, including in multilateral fora, on major foreign policy priorities.

title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment and Ammunition (PAE AS&A) and Army Sustainment Command (ASC) is hosting an Industry Day focused on transforming the operational strategy of Government Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) facilities on 17-19 November 2026 at the Lindner Conference Center, Picatinny, NJ. The Government will also provide an update on the Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) Energetics Center of Excellence (ECoE) at this event. The purpose of this Industry Day is to obtain Industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. The Government is seeking input from both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors as it explores transforming its operational strategy. The Government is seeking industry input on BGAD ECoE potential solutions achieving long-term self-sustainability, that would meet both defense and commercial needs, while providing resilience to the energetic organic industrial base. Schedule: The Government intends to host a 3-day event, consisting of a General Session and two subsequent days of one-on-one engagements. 17 November will be the General Session, which will consist of an open forum where Industry and Government discuss the topic areas identified in the GOCO and ECoE RFIs. 18 and 19 November will exclusively be one-on-one meetings with interested parties for both GOCO facility operations and the BGAD ECOE. The Government intends to have senior leaders and subject matter experts available for both the General Session and one-on-one engagements. A draft agenda for the General Session will be provided prior to the event. Instructions for Registration: Registration to attend is required, but attendance at the event is currently not limited per company. However, the Government reserves the right to further restrict attendance based on capacity restrictions, should the number of registrations exceed capacity of the venue. Registration for the event must be submitted via email by 30 October 2026 to usarmy.ria.acc.mbx.s3coe-events@army.mill. All interested participants must complete and provide the below information: Company Name and UEI/CAGE Name (First, Last, Middle Initial) and email address of each individual being registered Whether or not each registrant is a US Citizen If applicable, request for one-on-one engagement for either GOCO Strategy or BGAD ECOE, or both, with a mandatory description of the planned discussion topic(s) during the one-on-one. The Government will assign one-on-one breakouts based on the topic/level of engagement necessary. For GOCO Strategy one-on-one requests, please be specific which areas of consideration from the RFI below you are interested in discussing. If you have an alternate topic related to the overarching GOCO strategy, please detail it in your request. For the BGAD ECoE one-on-one requests, the intent is to discuss submitted RFI response and address any outstanding questions from both parties. In order to attend the event, registered individuals will need to bring a valid form of identification with them (REAL ID or passport) to access the facility. For both one-on-one opportunities, session durations will be tailored based on the scope of the proposed discussion topics and available time. . The Government will coordinate to ensure maximum participation, but due to availability of personnel and time slots, cannot guarantee all one-on-one requests will be granted. The Government will notify you of a scheduled one-on-one timeslot by COB 06 November. The Government is seeking Industry�s input to help shape the contents of the event. If you haven�t already, please respond to the questionnaire in this post relating to GOCO facility operations and/or to the BGAD ECOE RFI located at Notice ID: W519TC-26-R-0019 (https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/513aee5332ab4f1083396f8b658e7978/view). If you have any questions regarding the event, please reach out to the ACC-RI Source Selection Support Center of Excellence (S3COE) team at usarmy.ria.acc.mbx.s3coe-events@army.mill. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. Demand, Capacity, and Workload Management The Government seeks input on how Government requirements and approved non-Government workload can be integrated to improve plant utilization, responsiveness, and long-term viability. Modern, Flexible, and Resilient Production The Government seeks concepts for modernizing GOCO production capability to improve agility, resilience, and efficient response to changing demand. Topics may include: Flexible, modular, dual-use, and automated production lines; Rapid product changeover and qualification; Planned shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Automation, robotics, digital manufacturing, digital twins, and predictive maintenance; Equipment replacement, facility renewal, and obsolescence management; Workforce cross-training and critical-skill retention; Supply-chain resilience and access to existing U.S. industrial capacity; and Technical, regulatory, contractual, qualification, or facility barriers that limit modernization and flexibility. 4. title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability - CO2 Storage Vessel
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and inspection of a pressure vessel for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Storage Vessel (V-738). As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm?fixed price. The total anticipated duration for completion of all work is 28 weeks ARO, and the estimated sequential schedule is as follows: ASME Code design and analysis (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), WPS/PQR submittal and approval (3 weeks), complete shop fabrication including cleaning (25 weeks), install heating elements and insulate vessel (26 weeks), ship vessel to INL (27 weeks), and submission of the final Code Data Report, as?built drawings, and all other deliverables (28 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The vessel will be designed, fabricated, inspected, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The vessel, designated V-738, is a 200 cubic foot ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 code "U" stamped pressure vessel for gaseous CO2 service, with a design pressure of 1,800 psig and a design temperature range of -40�F to 500�F. The vessel is a horizontal configuration with two saddle supports spaced 16 feet apart, a 36-inch inner diameter, minimum 2-inch shell thickness, minimum 1-inch hemispherical head thickness, and an overall shell length of 26 feet 3-1/2 inches. The vessel includes seven nozzles (inlet, outlet, five inspection ports, a low point drain, a pressure relief nozzle, and two instrumentation ports), nine band heating elements (3.6 kW total) to maintain the vessel above 150�F, and Foamglas (or equivalent) insulation with protective aluminum sheathing. The vessel will be installed outdoors at INL in a high desert environment, with an altitude of 4,900 ft, ambient temperatures ranging from -40�F to 100�F, and exposure to wind, blowing sand, dust, snow, and frost. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Specific fabrication drawings, foundation details, and design calculations will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design and fabrication, including possession of a current "U" stamp certificate for both design and fabrication. Experience with stainless steel pressure vessel welding, including full penetration butt welds, 100% radiography, and carbide precipitation control during welding. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to fabricate the vessel in the required configuration, including nozzle arrangement, saddle supports, band heating elements, and insulation system. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including hydrostatic testing, positive material identification, liquid penetrant testing, and radiography or phased array ultrasonic testing. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Control System consistent with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 10. Compliance with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 47 requirements for pressure vessel design. Availability of a qualified and experienced project manager and Quality Control Manager to oversee the work. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley- Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability CO2 Compressor Design/Build
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and delivery of a CO2 compressor for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Compressor. As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm-fixed price. Per the proposed project schedule, all durations are After Receipt of Order (ARO): Engineering Documentation Report (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), complete shop fabrication (40 weeks), and compressor arrival at INL (3 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The compressor will be designed, fabricated, tested, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The compressor will be used to compress CO2 from a combustor unit into a storage vessel that will supply gas to downstream users, and will be housed in a protected shipping container. The compressor shall be oil-free, liquid-cooled, fixed speed, and electric motor driven. Inlet conditions are 50-100�F at 0.14-2 psig; outlet conditions are 1,400 psig, 66.1 scfm, and 150�F, with the unit operating on a nearly continuous basis. The compressor and all components must fit within a high cube shipping container with interior dimensions of 19'6" long x 7'9" wide x 8'10" high, and must be mounted on a structural frame designed and fabricated in accordance with the American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC), with welding per AWS D1.1. Any pressure vessels used in fabrication of the compressor must be designed and fabricated in accordance with ASME Section VIII, Division 1, and stamped and registered with the National Board. The compressor must withstand a CO2 gas stream composition of approximately 99% CO2 with trace nitrogen, oxygen, water vapor, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, hydrocarbons, hydrogen sulfide, and hydrogen chloride. The unit will be installed at INL at an altitude of approximately 4,938 ft, with a shipping container temperature range of 41�F to 104�F and humidity from 0 to 100%. The compressor package must include a control panel with instrumentation and alarms for conditions such as low discharge pressure and motor failure, a data history logging function, an emergency shutoff switch, and UL-508A listed control panels. The unit must be provided with inter-coolers or after-coolers to maintain outlet temperature at or below 150�F, and a stainless steel drip pan sized to contain at least 1.5 times the volume of any fluids contained in the compressor. Specific fabrication drawings, nozzle location diagrams, and design details will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in design and fabrication of oil-free, liquid-cooled CO2 or industrial gas compressor packages. Experience with ASME Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design where applicable to compressor components, and structural fabrication in accordance with AISC and AWS D1.1. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to package the compressor, motor, controls, and all interconnecting piping and instrumentation within the required shipping container footprint. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including non-destructive examination of castings and welds, operational testing, and a 10-hour continuous reliability test. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Assurance Plan based on a national consensus code such as ANSI/ASME ISO-9000. Capability to provide Operations & Maintenance documentation, a Recommended Spare Parts List, and field support for startup and commissioning. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley - Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

title: CFA-686 Carbon-based Fuels Capability - CO2 Storage Vessel
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to support the design, fabrication, testing, and inspection of a pressure vessel for the Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability. PROCESS BEA is seeking qualified firms to compete for the design/build contract in support of the CFA-686 CO2 Storage Vessel (V-738). As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that will require detailed technical and price proposals be provided for evaluation and ranking under a source selection process. Interested firms are advised that RFP release and the source selection/award decision timeline will be communicated following review of submitted EOIs. The contract award type will be firm-fixed price. Per the project schedule, all durations are After Receipt of Order (ARO): ASME Code design and analysis (3 weeks), shop fabrication drawings (4 weeks), WPS/PQR submittal and approval (3 weeks), complete shop fabrication including cleaning (25 weeks), install heating elements and insulate vessel (26 weeks), ship vessel to INL (27 weeks), and submission of the final Code Data Report, as-built drawings, and all other deliverables (28 weeks). PROJECT DESCRIPTION The vessel will be designed, fabricated, inspected, and delivered for the INL Central Facilities Area (CFA) Carbon-based Fuels Capability (CFA-686). The vessel, designated V-738, is a 200 cubic foot ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 code "U" stamped pressure vessel for gaseous CO2 service, with a design pressure of 1,800 psig and a design temperature range of -40�F to 500�F. The vessel is a horizontal configuration with two saddle supports spaced 16 feet apart, a 36-inch inner diameter, minimum 2-inch shell thickness, minimum 1-inch hemispherical head thickness, and an overall shell length of 26 feet 3-1/2 inches. The vessel includes seven nozzles (inlet, outlet, five inspection ports, a low point drain, a pressure relief nozzle, and two instrumentation ports), nine band heating elements (3.6 kW total) to maintain the vessel above 150�F, and Foamglas (or equivalent) insulation with protective aluminum sheathing. The vessel will be installed outdoors at INL in a high desert environment, with an altitude of 4,900 ft, ambient temperatures ranging from -40�F to 100�F, and exposure to wind, blowing sand, dust, snow, and frost. The vessel must be designed for static, seismic, and wind loading in accordance with IBC 2024, ASCE 7-10, and ACI 318-19, and fabricated from 304/304L stainless steel pressure boundary materials. Specific fabrication drawings, foundation details, and design calculations will be provided to qualified offerors as part of the RFP process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest to Chase Egbert (chase.egbert@inl.gov) by close-of-business on 10/16/2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder's qualifications addressing each of the following criteria: Experience in ASME BPVC Section VIII, Division 1 pressure vessel design and fabrication, including possession of a current "U" stamp certificate for both design and fabrication. Experience with stainless steel pressure vessel welding, including full penetration butt welds, 100% radiography, and carbide precipitation control during welding. Capability to meet the design/build schedule outlined above. Capability to fabricate the vessel in the required configuration, including nozzle arrangement, saddle supports, band heating elements, and insulation system. Proper identification and execution plan for inspection, examination, and testing, including hydrostatic testing, positive material identification, liquid penetrant testing, and radiography or phased array ultrasonic testing. Agreement to maintain a written Quality Control System consistent with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 10. Compliance with ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1, Mandatory Appendix 47 requirements for pressure vessel design. Availability of a qualified and experienced project manager and Quality Control Manager to oversee the work. Note that responses must be no more than 5 pages in length. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will receive the RFP for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in November 2026. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA Point of Contact, please contact the following via email: Project Manager - Ben Bryson - Benjamin.Bryson@inl.gov Project Engineer - Chris Dudley- Christopher.Dudley@inl.gov Technical questions must be submitted in writing via email.

title: Construct Small Arms Range - Presolicitation Notice
description: Amendment 01: Update Period of Performance and Brand Name requirements. No other changes were made: The New Hampshire Air National Guard intends to issue an Invitation for Bids to award a single firm fixed-price contract to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the Construction of a Small Arms Range (Project SZCQ1099041) at Pease ANGB, Newington, NH. The contract duration will be 455 calendar days after Notice to Proceed to include inspection and punch list. This project is set aside 100% for small business concerns. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is on-or-about 9 November 2026. The tentative date for the pre-bid conference will be listed in the SF 1442, typically 10 days after issuance of the solicitation. The bid closing will be a minimum of 30 days after solicitation issuance. The location and base access/registration requirements will be provided in the solicitation. A physical site visit of the Small Arms Range project location will immediately follow the pre-bid conference. The solicitation, associated information, plans, and specifications will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. Interested bidders must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). To register, go to www.SAM.gov. Instructions for registering are on the web page (there is no fee for registration). Your attention is directed to FAR clause 52.219-14(e)(3) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008, Revision 1), LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, which states �By submission of an offer and execution of a contract, the Offeror/Contractor agrees in performance of the contract for General construction, it will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor�s 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded�. In accordance with FAR 36.211(b), the following information is provided: (1) The National Guard has no agency-specific policies or procedures applicable to definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts other than those described at FAR 43.204, DFARS 243.204 and AFARS 5143.204. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Operations, Maintenance, and Defense of Army Communications - Southwest Asia (OMDAC-SWA) (Est. $206M)
description: The U.S. Government intends to negotiate and award a sole-source contract to V2X Systems LLC, Colorado Springs, CO, pursuant to the authority of RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The estimated value of this proposed action is $206 million (est.), including all options. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. At this time there is no recompete package which would include a new Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this notice. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: Comprehensive repair, preventive maintenance, technical sustainment, and operational support of military communication equipment, satellite networks, and associated infrastructure. The contractor must provide all management, personnel, administration, vehicles, travel, training, and equipment (except Government-Furnished Property) required to perform 24/7/365 sustainment, Operations and Maintenance (O&M), and repair of Army Base Communications Information Systems, tactical networks, and strategic communication equipment. Key technical areas focus on the repair and maintenance of: � Regional Cyber Center � SWA (RCC-SWA): Maintenance and technical support of Defensive Cyberspace Operations (DCO) systems, Wide Area Network (WAN)/LAN security hardware, Enterprise Systems Operations (SysOps) equipment, and database management systems. � Network Operations Centers (NOC): Repair, real-time monitoring, Level 1/2 troubleshooting, fault management, and circuit action support for active network equipment. � Strategic Transmission & Satellite Facilities: Technical maintenance and O&M of the Earth Terminal Complex (ETC) at Camp Arifjan, dual AN/GSC-39C DSCS antennas, Standardized Tactical Entry Point (STEP) terminal assets, and Regional Hub Node (RHN) systems. � Inside/Outside Plant (ISP/OSP): Technical O&M of switchboard systems, Command and Control Switching Systems (CCSS), DRSN hardware, and the physical repair and excavation of OSP fiber-optic/copper cable lines. � Infrastructure Support: Preventive maintenance and repair of communications supporting auxiliary power (emergency generators, fuel pods), large-scale Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS), and HVAC systems dedicated exclusively to strategic communication facilities. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Primarily Camp Arifjan, Kuwait, and other locations in the Southwest Asia (SWA) area of responsibility as required. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: This will be a 24-month action consisting of a 12-month base period and four (4) three-month option periods. Anticipated performance dates are as follows: Base: 01 November 2026 � 31 October 2027 Option 1: 01 November 2027 � 31 January 2028 Option 2: 01 February 2028 � 30 April 2028 Option 3: 01 May 2028 � 31 July 2028 Option 4: 01 August 2028 � 31 October 2028 INSTRUCTIONS TO INTERESTED PARTIES: Interested parties may submit a capability statement regarding this requirement by email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 19 October 2026 at 4:00 PM Arizona Time (UTC-7). Submissions shall be sent to: Audrey C. Hammonds, Contracting Officer audrey.c.hammonds.civ@army.mil Tammy A. Brewer, Contract Specialist tammy.a.brewer.civ@army.mil Note: The Government will not accept proposals in response to this notice.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – Sosiaalihuolto- ja lastensuojelulain mukaiset tukitoimet ja palvelut
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia sosiaalihuolto- ja lastensuojelulain mukaisista avohuollon tukitoimista ja palveluista ajalle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa optiot (1+1 vuotta) vuosille 2029 ja 2030. Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä viimeistään 12 kuukautta ennen alkuperäisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Osa-aluekohtaiset tarjoukset ovat sallittuja. Hankinta on jaettu osa-alueisiin: 1) Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelu Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelua järjestetään sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014 § 18 a) mukaisena palveluna. Kotipalvelulla tarkoitetaan asumiseen, hoitoon ja huolenpitoon, toimintakyvyn ylläpitoon, lasten hoitoon ja kasvatukseen, asiointiin sekä muihin jokapäiväiseen elämään kuuluvien tehtävien ja toimintojen suorittamista tai niissä avustamista. 2) Ammatillinen tukihenkilötoiminta Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa järjestetään lapsille, nuorille ja aikuisille. Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa voidaan järjestää sosiaalihuoltolain mukaisena palveluna (ShL1301/2014 § 28) ja tai osana lastensuojelun avohuoltoa (LsL 417/2007 § 36). Kainuun hyvinvointialue järjestää osa-alueiden mukaisia palveluja sekä omana toimintana että ostopalveluna. Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelussa pääpainopiste palveluntuottamisessa on omassa toiminnassa. Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa hankintaan ostopalveluna. Ammatillisen tukihenkilötoiminnan asiakasmäärät ja tukisuhteiden kestot vaihtelevat asiakkaiden palvelutarpeiden mukaisesti kaikissa asiakasryhmissä: aikuisasiakkaat, lastensuojelun jälkihuollossa olevat nuoret, lastensuojelun avohuollon asiakkailla ja sosiaalihuoltolain mukaisessa tukisuhdetoiminnassa olevilla lapsiasiakkailla. Tällä hetkellä lapsiperheiden sosiaalityössä ammatillinen tukihenkilö on noin sadalla asiakkaalla ja aikuisten sosiaalityössä noin kahdellakymmenellä asiakkaalla. Asiakasmäärä kuvaa nykytilannetta ja vaihtelee asiakkaiden yksilöllisten tuen tarpeiden mukaisesti. Asiakasmäärästä ei voi kuitenkaan tehdä johtopäätöstä tulevien vuosien määristä. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tarjouspyynnöllä tiettyyn hankintamäärään, eikä ole korvausvelvollinen mahdollisista hankintamäärän muutoksista sopimuskaudella. Tilaajan tarpeet voivat sopimuskauden aikana muuttua. Tarjouspyynnön asiakasmäärät ovat arvioita ja lopulliset hankittavan palvelun määrät voivat olla ilmoitettua suurempia tai pienempiä. Tilaajalla ei ole velvollisuutta maksaa palveluntuottajaan kohdistuvia mahdollisia maksuja. Mikäli hankintakauden aikana tulee lainsäädännöstä johtuvia tai muutoin Tilaajasta riippumattomista syistä muutoksia hankinnan kohteeseen, Tilaajan asemaan tai velvollisuuksiin, Tarjoaja sitoutuu siihen, että hankintasopimusta muutetaan niitä vastaavaksi. KORJAUSILMOITUKSEN SISÄLTÖ: Tilaaja täsmentää tällä korjausilmoituksella rinnakkaistarjouksen antamiseen liittyvää ohjetta sekä aiemmin antamaa vastausta lisäkysymykseen: "Saman Y-tunnuksen alla olevat useat yksiköt ilmoitetaan omina palveluyksiköinään, tilaaja vertailee yksikkökohtaisia tietoja. Tällöin kyse ei ole rinnakkaistarjouksesta vaan usean palveluyksikön tarjoamisesta. Kirjaus on lisätty 24.8.2026 tarjouspyynnön Muut vaatimukset- kohtaan". Edellä mainitussa tilanteessa kyse ON rinnakkaistarjouksesta eli useamman palveluyksikön tarjoaminen on mahdollista. Tarjoaja voi tehdä rinnakkaistarjouksen seuraavan ohjeen mukaisesti https://tuki.cloudia.fi/hc/fi/articles/4428294482065-Rinnakkainen-tarjous

title: Finland – Medical imaging services – Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen
description: Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia mammografiatutkimuspalveluista lausuntoineen Lapin hyvinvointialueen ja Työterveys Lappica Oy:n tarpeisiin. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen (2) osa-alueeseen, joista tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen joko yhteen tai molempiin: 1. Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Rovaniemellä: Palvelu tuotetaan Palveluntuottajan toimitiloissa Rovaniemellä. 2. Palvelutuotannon suunniteltu aloitusajankohta Rovaniemellä on 1.12.2026 ja Kemijärvellä 1.2.2027. Kyseessä on julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetun lain (1397/2016) 25 §:n 1 momentin 3 kohdan mukainen kansallisen kynnysarvon ylittävä liitteen E mukainen sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluhankinta. Tarjouspyyntö muodostuu tästä hankintailmoituksesta ja sen liitteistä.

title: Bulgaria – Miscellaneous evaluation or testing instruments – Доставка на оборудване и консумативи за лаборатория „Молекулярна биология“ по 5 обособени позиции
description: Предмет на настоящата обществена поръчка е доставка на специализирано лабораторно оборудване и консумативи за молекулярно-биологичен анализ, което да позволи на високо научно ниво да се дефинира влиянието на променливи фактори, обусловени от климатичните изменения, върху генетичния отговор на лозята, включително експресията на гени, свързани с устойчивост към биотичен и абиотичен стрес, както и ранно откриване на патогени (вируси, бактерии, фитоплазми и гъби) по лозата. Поръчката включва следните обособени позиции: Обособена позиция №1: „Доставка на консумативи за PCR и Real time PCR за текуща лабораторна работа“; Обособена позиция №2: „Доставка на ламинарни боксове (микробиологичен клас II А2 и за PCR) и лабораторна камина“; Обособена позиция № 3: „Доставка на общолабораторно оборудване“; Обособена позиция № 4: „Доставка на Автоклав“; Обособена позиция № 5: “Доставка на олигонуклеотиди (PCR праймери)”. ​​​​Дейността се финансира като част от проект „Адаптиране на лозарството към изменението на климата чрез прилагане на екосистемни мерки за поддържане на икономическата жизнеспособност (VitiClimRoBg–Hard ROBG00370)“, по Програма Interreg VI-A Румъния-България, специфична цел: 2.4 — Насърчаване на адаптирането към изменението на климата, предотвратяването на риска от бедствия и устойчивостта, като се вземат предвид екосистемни подходи. Специализираното оборудване, обект на настоящата обществена поръчка, е в интеграция с предходно заявени компоненти по проекта, за да се постигне интегриран комплексен подход, пряко обвързан с адаптацията към климатичните изменения. Целта е допълване на теренни и физикохимични данни с молекулярно-генетичен анализ, предоставящ прецизни, възпроизводими и научно обосновани резултати, които да очертаят връзката на климатичните изменения с генетичните механизми на адаптация на лозята, генерирайки последователно прилагане на устойчиви практики за „борба“ с климатичния отпечатък и установяване на икономическа жизнеспособност.

title: Fort McCoy Multipurpose Athletic Field Design-Build-to-Budget
description: A Market Survey is being conducted to gather information and feedback from the construction industry to help shape the acquisition strategy for this Design-Build-to-Budget project. The Government is seeking input from all interested business concerns, including Large Businesses, Small Businesses, and certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses. The information gathered will be used to refine the Government's procurement approach for this project delivery method and to determine the potential for a Small Business Set-Aside. If your firm is interested in this project as a prime contractor, please respond appropriately. Project Location: Fort McCoy, WI Project Title: Fort McCoy Multipurpose Athletic Field � Army Combat Fitness Testing Project Description: This project will be solicited as a Design-Build-to-Budget project. The purpose of this solicitation method is to maximize the achievable scope within a target budget ceiling (currently estimated at $14,676,000). The Design-Build to Budget project will consist of a contractual budget ceiling for which contractors will propose the quantities, configurations, construction type and other innovations that the proposing contractor can complete within the budget ceiling. Negotiations will occur with those offerors invited to Phase II to finalize the scope and cost after receipt of initial proposals. The goal is to allow maximum flexibility in design and construction. The Government intends to only include the basic requirements in the RFP. This will be a two (2) phase Design-Build procurement. Fort McCoy has no facility large enough to allow indoor Army�s Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) system activities or Army Fitness Test (AFT) testing in the winter months or during weather events. Currently outdoor activities are conducted on an existing Physical Training area consisting of an outdoor running track and a hand-to-hand combat training area. Students are required to complete the AFT outdoors in inhospitable conditions or must try to obtain a waiver for this component of their class. The site does not provide protected areas from the elements for the Soldiers during or in-between events. This project will utilize a Design-Build-to-Budget delivery method to design and construct a new facility to contain a 54,600 SF multipurpose athletic field at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin. The facility shall consist of a 200 meter rubberized running track and an artificial turf infield (sized according to Army Techniques Publication (ATP) 7-22.01 Holistic Health and Fitness Training requirements) for completing the annual Army Fitness Testing (AFT). Supporting facilities include site development, modification to existing improvements, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, sidewalks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Consistent temperature control inside the facility shall be provided by self-contained systems. ATFP measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Antiterrorism for Buildings will be provided. A life safety analysis of the facility shall be conducted to determine compliance with UFC, IBC, and NFPA codes and standards. A new addressable fire alarm system shall be installed in the facility that is compatible with the existing base fire alarm reporting system. Comprehensive building design services shall be required. Accessibility for individuals with disabilities shall be required. The multipurpose athletic field will be periodically occupied and shall require adequate clearance and circulation for personnel, maintenance and operations. Utility connections and telecommunications system(s) shall be coordinated. The facility shall be designed to a minimum life of 40 years and in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems performance. This is not a continuously used facility, and during periods of non-use utilities will be reduced or disconnected to conserve energy. The available funding for this project is capped at $14,676,000. Prospective offerors should design to, and propose a price that approaches, this maximum budget to maximize the technical value and betterments offered to the Government. Any proposal exceeding this $14,676,000 cap will be deemed non-compliant and ineligible for award. NAICS code is 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). All interested prime contractors should respond to this survey via email by 17 October 2026 by 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status under NAICS 236220 (Large Business, Small Business, and certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses) Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number and CAGE Code(s). Information on the Contractor�s ability to be bonded showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Descriptions of Experience � Interested construction firms must provide no more than three (3) example projects with either 95% completion or projects completed in the past six (6) years where the interested firm served as the Prime Contractor. Each project must include the following: a. Name b. Title c. Project Role d. Email Address e. Telephone Number f. At least one (1) reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages, and quality of performance. Documentation/Information demonstrating experience managing multiple sub-contractors. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. a. Projects similar in scope to this project include: (1) Artificial turf athletic fields, running tracks, building foundations. b. Projects similar in size to this project include: (1) Projects having a combined square footage of at least 40,000 SF. c. Based on the information above, for each project submitted, include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. (2) Size of the project (combined SF, acres of construction site, etc.) (3) Scope of the project (specific trades, site work, utility connections, mechanical systems, HVAC commissioning, roof systems, etc.) (4) The dollar value of the construction contract and project delivery method (whether it was Design-Bid Build, Design-Build, Design-Build-to-Budget, Progressive Design-Build, CMAR, etc.). (5) The portion and percentage of work that was self-performed. Describe the work your company self-performed. Must be at least 15% self-performed. Prescriptive "Showstoppers": Are there any requirements in our functional description that appear overly prescriptive or "locked-in" that might prevent you from offering a more innovative or cost-effective solution to meet the mission? Innovation Opportunities: In this building type, where do you typically see the most opportunity for an integrated design-build team to provide "more for the money" (e.g., modular systems, envelope efficiency, MEP coordination)? Long-Lead Warning: Even without a full design, are there specific systems common to this facility type (e.g., generators, custom AHUs, specialized equipment) that are currently experiencing lead times that would threaten the proposed project schedule? Local Labor Constraints: Are there specific trades in the project area that are currently over-extended or in short supply that could impact the project's risk profile? title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Award M.C. Dean
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE TO: M.C. DEAN, INC. (UEI:RD55NEXJ5EW4 / CAGE:3K773) Joint Base Andrews has a requirement to procure, install, and integrate a comprehensive Security Management System for a specific facility. Major items include high-definition cameras, PIV-class card readers, Servers, Server Software and Licenses. The required components and service for integration in the current proprietary intrusion detection system are provided by M.C. Dean Inc. Air Force physical security standards and Integrated Base Defense Security System (IBDSS) guidelines mandate that all electronic security systems, intrusion detection systems, and access control platforms maintain strict Department of Defense (DoD) Joint Services Interior Security Commission (JSIDS) and USAF Protection Level 1 (PL-1) non-nuclear security certifications. Only items fully certified and compatible with the existing base head-end software and network backbone are authorized for installation and integration. While competition for various security requirements exist, market research conducted by the Government revealed only one responsible vendor would be able to support this effort due to the vital, pre-established integrated security functions and nature of facility operations. In addition to sensitive operations at Joint Base Andrews, site surveys were limited to approved GSA vendors to minimize risk while protecting critical national security information. The government will continue to monitor the updated Air Force certified equipment lists for all future purchases of this nature to verify if competition is available to include sourcing potential Governmentwide acquisition contracts and other approved vehicles. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the government. Vendors that believe they can provide the items listed above are invited to submit substantiating documentation in writing to the identified point of contact. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the government to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the government.

title: 12 Month Service maintenance for Cytek Aurora flow cytometer
description: NOI-NIAID-26-2278150 NAICS � 811210 This is a Notice of Intent notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This critical procurement is to purchase Service maintenance for the Cytek Aurora flow cytometer. This is necessary purchasing for our ongoing research experiments that began before January 20, 2025, and are directly related to human healthcare as they are aimed at the identification of most effective protocols for production of HIV envelope protein for vaccine use. These items are for an ongoing project related to our active research project entitled �Structure-Function Studies of the HIV-1 Envelope Glycoproteins�(ZIA AI001197-09), whose scope is to elucidate the structure-function relations in the HIV-1 envelope. To ensure timely action on this project, the items in this procurement must be purchased because the materials are related to patient samples, and we risk compromising the entire experiment if they are not purchased in time. This is a Notice of Intent; the National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate a sole source contract for the maintenance agreement with: CYTEK BIOSCIENCES INC The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302.1(b)(1)(i) �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency Requirements.�, no substitutions possible. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities, https://www.sam.gov. REQUIREMENT: The Cytek Biosciences provides timely, cost efficiently and most reliably On-Site Flow Cytometry Services that includes - Maintenance and Repair - Service maintenance for the Cytek Aurora flow cytometer ensures the optical alignment, fluidics, and unmixing algorithms work flawlessly. This is critical for T cell and B cell research, which relies on resolving 40+ marker panels , separating dim and rare cell subsets, and extracting high autofluorescence . Cytek Aurora flow cytometer is the most important instrument for our ongoing research experiments that began before January 20, 2025, and are directly related to human healthcare as they are aimed at the identification of most effective protocols for production of HIV envelope protein for vaccine use. REQUIREMENTS: Cytek Biosciences offers multi-tiered On-Site Services and Repair Plans for the Cytek Aurora, with preventative maintenance performed primarily by Field Service Engineers . Key Labor Categories Field Service Engineer (FSE): The primary labor category. These are OEM factory-trained technicians who conduct on-site preventive maintenance, hardware diagnostics, and emergency repairs. Technical Applications Specialist (TAS): A secondary support labor category for remote or on-site support. These specialists assist with assay optimization, general scientific consultation, panel design, and troubleshooting. Only one award will be made as a result of this notice, and the award will be a Firm-Fixed price purchase order. This will be the only notice of the Government�s intent to solicit, negotiate, and award to one source to satisfy this requirement. The Government plans to award a purchase order for this requirement within five (5) days of closing this notice. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTATIONS. All responsible, qualified sources who can provide the equipment and service should submit a capability statement electronically to the Contracting Officer, Linda Smith at linda.smith2@nih.gov and Acquisition Specialist, Jessica Emerson (Contractor Support) at jessica.emerson@nih.gov by 2:00 PM EST on October 18, 2026. Facsimile responses are NOT accepted. Any responses received by NIH after this date and exact time specified are late and will not be considered. The determination to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. title: Holter-palveluiden hankinta
description: Holter-palveluiden hankinta Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia Holter -palveluista Kainuun keskussairaalaan sisätaudeille ja lastentaudeille sekä Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveysasemille erikoissairaanhoidon toimintana. Arvioitu sopimuskausi on 1.3.2027- 28.2.2029. Sopimuskausi alkaa, kun molemmat sopijapuolet ovat allekirjoittaneet sopimuksen ja kestää kaksi (2) vuotta. Lisäksi tilaaja varaa option 1 + 1 vuodelle. Palveluun sisältyvät laitteisto, automaattinen tiedonsiirto, analysointi ja kardiologian lausunto. Holter-rekisteröintilaitteista vastaa palveluntuottaja. Laitteen luovuttaa asiakkaalle hoitaja joko Kainuun keskussairaalan sisätautien poliklinikalta tai Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveyskeskuksista. Asiakas palauttaa laitteen hoitohenkilökunnalle, joka purkaa rekisteröinnin ja esitiedot palveluntuottajan sähköiseen järjestelmään/palveluun. Lausunto tulee olla sähköisessä muodossa ja potilaan oirepäiväkirja tulee olla suoraan analyysipalveluun liitettävä. Rekisteröinnin tulee tapahtua ilman henkilötietoja. Tallenteiden purkaminen ei vaadi käyttäjältä erillistä ohjelmistoa tallenteiden käsittelyyn vaan raakatallenteet lähetetään palveluntuottajalle rekisteröintijärjestelmän sivuston kautta. Hoitava lääkäri saa selkeän lausunnon jatkosuosituksineen pdf-tiedostona ja lausunto tulee olla liitettävissä potilaan tietoihin järjestelmään: Commitwebb; kuva-arkisto Sectra IDS7:ään. Palvelulle asetetut vaatimukset esitetty tarjouspyynnön Muut ehdot ja Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit kohdissa. Holter-laitteiden tarve Kainuun hyvinvointialueelle on kaiken kaikkiaan 11 laitetta (sisältäen Kainuun keskussairaalan, jokaisen Kainuun alueen terveyskeskuksen ja lasten laitteiden tarpeet).,

title: Sosiaalihuolto- ja lastensuojelulain mukaiset tukitoimet ja palvelut
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia sosiaalihuolto- ja lastensuojelulain mukaisista avohuollon tukitoimista ja palveluista ajalle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2028. Lisäksi Tilaaja varaa optiot (1+1 vuotta) vuosille 2029 ja 2030. Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä viimeistään 12 kuukautta ennen alkuperäisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Osa-aluekohtaiset tarjoukset ovat sallittuja. Hankinta on jaettu osa-alueisiin: 1) Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelu Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelua järjestetään sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014 § 18 a) mukaisena palveluna. Kotipalvelulla tarkoitetaan asumiseen, hoitoon ja huolenpitoon, toimintakyvyn ylläpitoon, lasten hoitoon ja kasvatukseen, asiointiin sekä muihin jokapäiväiseen elämään kuuluvien tehtävien ja toimintojen suorittamista tai niissä avustamista. 2) Ammatillinen tukihenkilötoiminta Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa järjestetään lapsille, nuorille ja aikuisille. Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa voidaan järjestää sosiaalihuoltolain mukaisena palveluna (ShL1301/2014 § 28) ja tai osana lastensuojelun avohuoltoa (LsL 417/2007 § 36). Kainuun hyvinvointialue järjestää osa-alueiden mukaisia palveluja sekä omana toimintana että ostopalveluna. Lapsiperheiden kotipalvelussa pääpainopiste palveluntuottamisessa on omassa toiminnassa. Ammatillista tukihenkilötoimintaa hankintaan ostopalveluna. Ammatillisen tukihenkilötoiminnan asiakasmäärät ja tukisuhteiden kestot vaihtelevat asiakkaiden palvelutarpeiden mukaisesti kaikissa asiakasryhmissä: aikuisasiakkaat, lastensuojelun jälkihuollossa olevat nuoret, lastensuojelun avohuollon asiakkailla ja sosiaalihuoltolain mukaisessa tukisuhdetoiminnassa olevilla lapsiasiakkailla. Tällä hetkellä lapsiperheiden sosiaalityössä ammatillinen tukihenkilö on noin sadalla asiakkaalla ja aikuisten sosiaalityössä noin kahdellakymmenellä asiakkaalla. Asiakasmäärä kuvaa nykytilannetta ja vaihtelee asiakkaiden yksilöllisten tuen tarpeiden mukaisesti. Asiakasmäärästä ei voi kuitenkaan tehdä johtopäätöstä tulevien vuosien määristä. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tarjouspyynnöllä tiettyyn hankintamäärään, eikä ole korvausvelvollinen mahdollisista hankintamäärän muutoksista sopimuskaudella. Tilaajan tarpeet voivat sopimuskauden aikana muuttua. Tarjouspyynnön asiakasmäärät ovat arvioita ja lopulliset hankittavan palvelun määrät voivat olla ilmoitettua suurempia tai pienempiä. title: Holter-palveluiden hankinta
description: Holter-palveluiden hankinta Kainuun hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia Holter -palveluista Kainuun keskussairaalaan sisätaudeille ja lastentaudeille sekä Suomussalmen, Kuhmon, Puolangan ja Sotkamon terveysasemille erikoissairaanhoidon toimintana. Arvioitu sopimuskausi on 1.3.2027- 28.2.2029. Sopimuskausi alkaa, kun molemmat sopijapuolet ovat allekirjoittaneet sopimuksen ja kestää kaksi (2) vuotta. Lisäksi tilaaja varaa option 1 + 1 vuodelle. Palveluun sisältyvät laitteisto, automaattinen tiedonsiirto, analysointi ja kardiologian lausunto. Holter-rekisteröintilaitteista vastaa palveluntuottaja. Lausunto tulee olla sähköisessä muodossa ja potilaan oirepäiväkirja tulee olla suoraan analyysipalveluun liitettävä. Rekisteröinnin tulee tapahtua ilman henkilötietoja. Tallenteiden purkaminen ei vaadi käyttäjältä erillistä ohjelmistoa tallenteiden käsittelyyn vaan raakatallenteet lähetetään palveluntuottajalle rekisteröintijärjestelmän sivuston kautta.
